title: The Hermitian inner product selects the time axis, the Born rule measures it
summary: The correspondence between $2\times 2$ Hermitian matrices and Minkowski $4$-vectors recovers Lorentzian symmetries from the internal degrees of freedom of a qubit, with no reference to an external spacetime. Recent work characterises the resulting Lorentz invariants and leaves the \emph{mechanism} of emergence -- what singles out a time direction -- as an explicit open question. We give an elementary answer and, in doing so, correct a natural misattribution. The bare spin space $(\mathbb{C}^2,\varepsilon)$ is $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$-symmetric and singles out no axis; so is the null cone it generates. What selects a future-timelike axis is the choice of a Hermitian inner product, equivalently a positive reference form $σ^0$: this choice -- made in passing from a normed space to a Hilbert space, \emph{before} any probability is assigned -- reduces $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ to its maximal compact $SU(2)$, the stabiliser of $σ^0$. The Born rule enters one level later: $\langle ξ\vert ξ\rangle = \text{tr}(σ^0 \, ξξ^\dagger)$ is the projection of the state's null vector onto $σ^0$, i.e. its energy in that frame, and under a boost it rescales as a Doppler shift. Thus the Hilbert structure selects the axis; the Born rule is where that axis becomes a measurable energy and where the frame-dependence of $\lvertψ\rvert^2$ becomes empirical. The ingredients are classical; what we add is their identification as the mechanism the recent programme leaves open, with the symmetry-breaking step located precisely. This is a kinematic identification of that step, not a dynamical account of why a particular axis is selected. We close by handing back the many-qubit case, where the datum is a tuple of such choices.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies the mechanism by which a time direction emerges from the SL(2,C)-symmetric spin space of a qubit: the choice of a Hermitian inner product (a positive reference form σ⁰) breaks the symmetry to SU(2), selecting a future-timelike axis. The Born rule then projects state null vectors onto this axis, giving energy and frame-dependent probability. This corrects a common misattribution in the literature.
AI.motivation: To resolve an open question in the recent programme on Lorentzian emergence from qubit internal degrees of freedom: what mechanism singles out a time direction, and to correct a natural misattribution about where this symmetry-breaking occurs.
AI.method: Elementary kinematic analysis of the spin space (ℂ², ε) showing that the choice of a Hermitian inner product (σ⁰) reduces SL(2,C) to SU(2), selecting a future-timelike axis; the Born rule is then reinterpreted as projection onto that axis.
AI.result: The Hilbert space structure (choice of Hermitian inner product) selects the time axis; the Born rule makes that axis empirically measurable as energy and accounts for frame-dependence of |ψ|² via Doppler shifts under boosts.
AI.conclusion: The symmetry-breaking step is precisely located at the transition from a normed space to a Hilbert space, before probability assignment. This is a kinematic identification, not a dynamical explanation, and extends naturally to the many-qubit case where the datum is a tuple of such choices.

title: Against Totalitarianism -- Introduction to Tractatus Quanticum
summary: Tractatus Quanticum (arXiv:2512.06034 [quant-ph]) is described by its authors as 'a re-editing, which takes quantum mechanics into account, of Wittgenstein's famous Tractatus.' The original Tractatus appeared with an introduction by Bertrand Russell. For Tractatus Quanticum, that role fell to us. This is the result.

AI.tldr: This paper presents Tractatus Quanticum, a re-editing of Wittgenstein's Tractatus that incorporates quantum mechanics, with an introduction written by the authors.
AI.motivation: To reinterpret Wittgenstein's philosophical work through the lens of quantum mechanics.
AI.method: Re-editing Wittgenstein's original Tractatus to account for quantum mechanical principles.
AI.result: The introduction to Tractatus Quanticum written by the authors.
AI.conclusion: The paper serves as the introductory material commissioned for this quantum-informed reinterpretation of Wittgenstein's work.

title: Lean-Quantum: Toward AI-Assisted Formalization of Quantum Information
comment: 34 pages, the Lean library is available at https://github.com/Hayata-Yamasaki-Group/lean-quantum
summary: Quantum information theory is built on entropic quantities; among them, the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy is a fundamental divergence with various applications, and its data processing inequality (DPI) under quantum channels is a cornerstone result. In this work, we present a Lean 4 library for quantum information, designed as a reusable formal infrastructure for theoretical analysis. As a central demonstration of the library, we formalize the DPI for the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy for positive semidefinite operators on finite-dimensional quantum systems. The library provides a basis-independent operator-theoretic framework for finite-dimensional quantum mechanics compatible with the standard mathematical library Mathlib, including reusable interfaces for finite-dimensional systems, states, channels, tensor products, partial traces, Choi operators, Kraus representations, and Stinespring representations. It also builds infrastructure for noncommutative trace inequalities, including operator monotonicity and convexity via the real continuous functional calculus, block-operator positivity, Hilbert-Schmidt operator spaces, Jensen's operator inequality, generalized perspectives, operator power means, and Lieb-Ando trace inequalities. On top of this framework, we formalize entropy-specific ingredients for the DPI: variational formulas for the sandwiched quasi-entropy via Young and reverse-Young inequalities, tensor-product compatibility of real powers, and Haar measures on unitary groups. Together, these components yield a Lean formalization of the DPI, give strong subadditivity as a corollary, and provide the last missing component needed to complete the Lean formalization of the generalized quantum Stein's lemma. More broadly, the development provides machine-checkable foundations for future formalized and AI-assisted research in quantum information theory.

AI.tldr: This work presents a Lean 4 library for quantum information theory, formalizing operator-theoretic foundations (states, channels, tensor products, etc.) and trace inequalities (operator monotonicity, Jensen's inequality, Lieb-Ando inequalities). As a central result, it formalizes the data processing inequality (DPI) for sandwiched Rényi relative entropy, with strong subadditivity as a corollary, completing the final component needed for the Lean formalization of the generalized quantum Stein's lemma.
AI.motivation: To provide machine-checkable, reusable formal infrastructure for quantum information theory in Lean 4, enabling rigorous verification of core results and supporting future formalized and AI-assisted research.
AI.method: The authors built a basis-independent operator-theoretic framework in Lean 4 compatible with Mathlib, covering finite-dimensional quantum systems, states, channels, tensor products, partial traces, Choi operators, Kraus/Stinespring representations, noncommutative trace inequalities (operator monotonicity/convexity via real continuous functional calculus, Jensen's operator inequality, generalized perspectives, operator power means, Lieb-Ando trace inequalities), and entropy-specific ingredients (variational formulas via Young/reverse-Young inequalities, tensor-product compatibility of real powers, Haar measures on unitary groups).
AI.result: Formalized the DPI for sandwiched Rényi relative entropy for positive semidefinite operators on finite-dimensional systems; derived strong subadditivity as a corollary; provided the last missing component to complete the Lean formalization of the generalized quantum Stein's lemma.
AI.conclusion: The library establishes a reusable, machine-checkable foundation for quantum information theory in Lean 4, enabling future formalized and AI-assisted research in the field.

title: Towards Lattice Surgery Compilation for the Color Code Using Pipe Diagrams
summary: Pipe diagrams have emerged as a powerful framework for flexible lattice surgery compilation and spacetime optimization for the surface code. In contrast, analogous compilation techniques for color code architectures remain largely unexplored, despite the color code's favorable properties, including reduced qubit overhead and transversal single-qubit Clifford gates. In this work, we develop a pipe diagram representation for the triangular color code on the 6.6.6 lattice and establish its correspondence to ZX-diagrammatic descriptions of computation. We present distance-independent constructions of color code pipe diagrams together with explicit realizations of correlation surfaces, stabilizers, and syndrome extraction circuits. This framework enables both macroscopic optimization of logical computations in spacetime and microscopic compilation to executable syndrome extraction circuits. We demonstrate the potential for compact spacetime embeddings with the color code's geometry. These results provide a foundation for automated lattice surgery compilation and diagrammatic optimization in color code architectures.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a pipe diagram representation for triangular color codes on the 6.6.6 lattice, linking it to ZX-diagrams, and provides distance-independent constructions of pipe diagrams with explicit correlation surfaces, stabilizers, and syndrome extraction circuits, enabling spacetime optimization and automated lattice surgery compilation for color code architectures.
AI.motivation: While pipe diagrams have been successfully used for flexible lattice surgery compilation in surface codes, analogous techniques for color code architectures remain unexplored, despite the color code's advantages such as reduced qubit overhead and transversal single-qubit Clifford gates.
AI.method: The authors develop a pipe diagram representation for the triangular color code on the 6.6.6 lattice, establish its correspondence to ZX-diagrammatic descriptions, and present distance-independent constructions of pipe diagrams with explicit realizations of correlation surfaces, stabilizers, and syndrome extraction circuits.
AI.result: The framework enables both macroscopic spacetime optimization of logical computations and microscopic compilation to executable syndrome extraction circuits, demonstrating potential for compact spacetime embeddings using the color code's geometry.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a foundation for automated lattice surgery compilation and diagrammatic optimization in color code architectures.

title: Autoencoder-Based Unsupervised Identification of Nonequilibrium Phases in Sheared Binary Colloids
summary: Identifying nonequilibrium phases in particle systems remains a major challenge because they often exhibit complex and spatially heterogeneous structures without long-range order. Here, we develop an unsupervised machine-learning framework for classifying such nonequilibrium phases by integrating Fourier-based preprocessing, an autoencoder, and a Gaussian mixture model (GMM). Specifically, we transform global spatial configurations into Fourier space and use the amplitudes of Fourier coefficients as inputs to the autoencoder. This preprocessing suppresses spatial noise while preserving phase-specific structural features and physical interpretability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework using a binary charged colloidal system under steady shear flow, where the competition between Coulomb interactions and shear gives rise to three nonequilibrium phases characterized by distinct local structures. The encoded latent space reveals well-separated clusters that are robustly identified by the GMM, enabling the construction of a nonequilibrium phase diagram based on cluster membership probabilities. The resulting phase boundaries are consistent with those independently obtained from radial distribution function analysis and unsupervised anomaly detection. These results demonstrate that autoencoder-based unsupervised learning provides an effective framework for identifying nonequilibrium phases in complex particle systems.

AI.tldr: The paper develops an unsupervised ML framework combining Fourier preprocessing, an autoencoder, and a GMM to classify nonequilibrium phases in particle systems, demonstrated on a binary charged colloidal system under shear flow.
AI.motivation: Identifying nonequilibrium phases in particle systems is challenging due to their complex, spatially heterogeneous structures without long-range order.
AI.method: The framework integrates Fourier-based preprocessing (transforming spatial configurations to Fourier space and using amplitude coefficients), an autoencoder for dimensionality reduction, and a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) for clustering in the latent space.
AI.result: The latent space exhibits well-separated clusters robustly identified by GMM, enabling construction of a nonequilibrium phase diagram based on cluster membership probabilities. Phase boundaries align with those from radial distribution function analysis and unsupervised anomaly detection.
AI.conclusion: Autoencoder-based unsupervised learning provides an effective framework for identifying nonequilibrium phases in complex particle systems.

title: Low-depth simulation of non-Markovianity under quantum hardware noise
summary: Simulating open quantum systems on digital quantum computers typically relies on the use of auxiliary qubits, resulting in overheads of noisy multi-qubit gates, that severely limit execution on near-term hardware. In this work, we explore the simulation of non-Markovian dynamics as well as memory channels leveraging the method of trajectory mixing, valid for mixed unitary channels. This allows to drastically reduce circuit depth, trading entangling gates for a statistical mixture of independent, pure state trajectories. Using a realistic noise model calibrated to modern quantum processors, we show the benefits of this approach, yielding higher state fidelity and better preservation of quantum correlations. This shows the possibility of simulating long-time non-Markovian evolutions with low noise and limited resources.

AI.tldr: The paper explores trajectory mixing to simulate non-Markovian open quantum systems on digital quantum computers, replacing deep entangling circuits with statistical mixtures of pure-state trajectories, demonstrating higher fidelity and better quantum correlation preservation under realistic noise models.
AI.motivation: Simulating open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware is severely limited by the overhead of noisy multi-qubit gates required by auxiliary-qubit-based approaches.
AI.method: The authors leverage trajectory mixing, valid for mixed unitary channels, which replaces entangling gates with a statistical mixture of independent pure-state trajectories.
AI.result: Using a realistic noise model calibrated to modern quantum processors, the trajectory mixing approach yields higher state fidelity and better preservation of quantum correlations compared to standard methods.
AI.conclusion: Trajectory mixing enables simulation of long-time non-Markovian evolutions with low noise and limited resources on near-term quantum hardware.

title: Electron-Phonon Dephasing in Ultrathin Disordered Films: From Power Laws to Diagnostic Maps
summary:
Electron-phonon dephasing in ultrathin disordered metallic films is often summarized by a power law, $τ_{e-ph}^{-1}=AT^p$. However, thin metals, alloys, and superconducting films exhibit effective exponents close to 2, 3, and 4, as well as intermediate nonuniversal values. We argue that in ultrathin supported films, the exponent should be treated not as a universal material constant, but as a crossover observable. Its interpretation requires several coordinates: the clean-to-dirty parameter $q_T l$, phonon confinement and film-substrate acoustic coupling, and the microscopic character of disorder.
  The diagnostic picture is illustrated using Ar-ion-irradiated Au films as a controlled-disorder series. In these films, the fitted electron-phonon exponent remains near $p\simeq 2$ for low values of the pure-dirty crossover temperature $T_{tr}\simeq \hbar s/(k_B l)$ and increases toward $p\simeq 2.8$ as disorder increases. At the same time, the prefactor trend indicates suppression of electron-phonon scattering with decreasing mean free path, consistent with dirty-limit weakening rather than static-disorder enhancement. The persistence of $p<4$ points to the role of thin-film or film-substrate phonon effects. The resulting diagnostic map provides a compact framework for comparing electron-phonon dephasing data in ultrathin disordered films.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that the power-law exponent for electron-phonon dephasing in ultrathin disordered metallic films is not a universal constant but a crossover observable, influenced by disorder, phonon confinement, and film-substrate coupling. Using Ar-ion-irradiated Au films, they show the exponent increases from p≈2 to p≈2.8 with increasing disorder, while the prefactor suppression indicates dirty-limit weakening.
AI.motivation: The observed non-universal exponents (near 2, 3, 4, or intermediate) in various thin films cannot be explained by a single universal power law. The authors aim to establish a framework treating the exponent as a crossover observable dependent on multiple physical parameters.
AI.method: The authors use Ar-ion-irradiated Au films as a controlled-disorder series, measuring electron-phonon dephasing across varying disorder levels. They analyze the fitted exponent and prefactor trends relative to the crossover temperature T_tr and mean free path.
AI.result: For low disorder (low T_tr), the exponent remains near p≈2. As disorder increases, the exponent rises toward p≈2.8. The prefactor trend shows suppression of e-ph scattering with decreasing mean free path, indicating dirty-limit weakening. The exponent remains below p<4, pointing to thin-film or substrate phonon effects.
AI.conclusion: The electron-phonon exponent should be interpreted as a crossover observable rather than a universal constant. A diagnostic map incorporating the clean-to-dirty parameter, phonon confinement, and film-substrate coupling provides a compact framework for comparing data across ultrathin disordered films.

title: Reduced Quantum-Reference-Frame Channels for Open Quantum Systems
summary: When reference frames are treated quantum mechanically, the subsystem structure of quantum systems is no longer absolute, but depends on the choice of the quantum reference frame (QRF). This raises a basic question: which dynamical properties are preserved across QRFs, and which depend on the physical reference used to define the system? We study this question in the general setting of open quantum systems. At the operational level, after a QRF transformation, the old reference frame and environmental degrees of freedom may be inaccessible and must therefore be traced out. This motivates the definition of reduced quantum-reference-frame channels: maps that connect the joint description in one frame to the accessible subsystem in another. We characterize their symmetry-constrained structure and define a regime in which a reduced entropy-coherence conservation law holds. We also identify when the induced reduced action on the open system admits a classical interpretation as random frame misalignment, and when it instead reflects quantum reduced-frame effects. We then apply the framework to pure-dephasing dynamics and derive a necessary and sufficient compatibility condition for population preservation. When the frame symmetry commutes with the open system's free Hamiltonian, coherences acquire a multiplicative frame factor, so that locally inferred decoherence rates split into environmental and reference-induced contributions. Ramsey interferometry gives this split a direct operational meaning. Finally, a gravity-motivated dephasing model illustrates how degradation of a phase reference can mimic signatures usually attributed to intrinsic decoherence mechanisms.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how open quantum system dynamics transform under changes of quantum reference frames (QRFs), defining reduced QRF channels that account for tracing out inaccessible frame/environment degrees of freedom. It identifies a regime with an entropy-coherence conservation law, distinguishes classical vs quantum reduced-frame effects, derives compatibility conditions for population preservation, shows that coherences acquire multiplicative frame factors splitting decoherence rates into environmental and reference-induced contributions, and demonstrates that phase reference degradation can mimic intrinsic decoherence in gravity-motivated models.
AI.motivation: Quantum reference frames make subsystem structure frame-dependent, raising the question of which dynamical properties are preserved across QRFs and which depend on the physical reference used to define the system.
AI.method: The paper adopts an operational open quantum systems approach, defining reduced QRF channels that connect joint descriptions in one frame to accessible subsystems in another after tracing out inaccessible frame and environment degrees of freedom. It characterizes symmetry-constrained structures, analyzes entropy-coherence conservation, distinguishes classical vs quantum reduced-frame effects, and applies the framework to pure-dephasing dynamics and a gravity-motivated dephasing model.
AI.result: A regime with a reduced entropy-coherence conservation law is identified. A necessary and sufficient compatibility condition for population preservation under pure-dephasing dynamics is derived. Coherences acquire multiplicative frame factors that split decoherence rates into environmental and reference-induced contributions, with operational meaning via Ramsey interferometry. Phase reference degradation in gravity-motivated models can mimic intrinsic decoherence signatures.
AI.conclusion: The choice of QRF fundamentally affects the dynamical description of open quantum systems; reference-induced decoherence effects can be indistinguishable from environmental decoherence, which is crucial for interpreting experiments in quantum gravity and quantum information.

title: Entanglement Entropy of Free Fermions on Random Fractal Lattices
summary: Random fractal lattices provide a geometrically disordered setting in which quantum correlations can be shaped by noninteger dimensionality rather than onsite randomness. We investigate the entanglement properties of noninteracting fermions on random fractal lattices generated by a stochastic growth algorithm. By varying the growth parameter and adding missing links with probability $p$, we tune the Hausdorff and spectral dimensions while keeping the system free of onsite disorder. For ground states at different fillings, we compute the bipartite entanglement entropy of subregions defined by graph distance and analyze its scaling with subsystem size. Over a broad parameter range, we find robust power-law behavior governed primarily by the Hausdorff dimension, consistent with a generalized area law and without the logarithmic enhancement familiar from Euclidean free fermions. We also study entanglement growth following a global quench from an uncorrelated checkerboard state and uncover an asymptotic scaling collapse in which the subsystem-size dependence is governed by the Hausdorff dimension, while the temporal evolution is governed by the spectral dimension. The resulting dynamics are logarithmically slow over an extended intermediate-time window. These results show that geometric randomness alone can generate both nontrivial ground-state entanglement structure and slow quantum-information spreading in free-fermion systems.

AI.tldr: This paper studies entanglement in noninteracting fermions on random fractal lattices without onsite disorder. Ground-state entanglement entropy scales as a power law governed by the Hausdorff dimension (no logarithmic enhancement). Post-quench entanglement dynamics show scaling collapse where subsystem-size dependence is set by Hausdorff dimension and temporal evolution by spectral dimension, yielding logarithmically slow spreading.
AI.motivation: To understand how geometric randomness (noninteger dimensionality) alone shapes quantum correlations and entanglement, independent of conventional onsite disorder, in free-fermion systems.
AI.method: Random fractal lattices are generated via a stochastic growth algorithm with tunable Hausdorff and spectral dimensions (via growth parameter and missing-link probability p). Bipartite entanglement entropy is computed for ground states at various fillings and for post-quench dynamics from a checkerboard state, using graph-distance-based subregions.
AI.result: Ground-state entanglement entropy follows robust power-law scaling with subsystem size, governed primarily by Hausdorff dimension, without the logarithmic enhancement seen in Euclidean free fermions. Post-quench dynamics exhibit asymptotic scaling collapse: subsystem-size dependence controlled by Hausdorff dimension, temporal evolution by spectral dimension, with logarithmically slow growth over an extended intermediate-time window.
AI.conclusion: Geometric randomness alone can produce nontrivial ground-state entanglement structures and slow quantum-information spreading in free-fermion systems, establishing random fractal lattices as a platform for disorder-free noninteger-dimensional quantum correlations.

title: Nonlocal transfer of quantized toroidal magnetic flux
summary: We propose a nonlocal flux-transfer experiment in which a quantized magnetic-field excitation confined within one toroidal superconducting structure is coherently transferred to a spatially separated toroid without magnetic-field occupation of the intervening region. The transfer arises from quantized Aharonov-Bohm-type vector potential coupling mediated by a superconducting loop threading the toroids, which, however, remains in the ground state, acting only through a global fluxoid constraint. A direct experimental signature would be the observation of correlated, time-resolved flux exchange between remote toroids in a SQUID readout. We analyze an apparent signaling paradox related to this interaction as a probe of the broader question of whether spatiotemporal quantum coherence is fundamentally bounded. The proposed setup can provide an experimental testbed for addressing foundational questions such as the existence of an objective collapse of a wavefunction or the fundamental limits of macroscopic quantum coherence which is relevant to large scale quantum computers.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a nonlocal flux-transfer experiment between two toroidal superconductors mediated by a superconducting loop in its ground state, enabling fluxoid transfer via Aharonov-Bohm-type coupling without magnetic field occupation of the intervening region. The setup could test foundational quantum questions like objective collapse and macroscopic coherence limits.
AI.motivation: To probe the fundamental bounds of spatiotemporal quantum coherence by designing a nonlocal, mediated flux transfer between remote toroids that avoids direct magnetic field propagation, and to address foundational questions such as objective wavefunction collapse and macroscopic quantum coherence limits relevant to large-scale quantum computing.
AI.method: A nonlocal flux-transfer experiment using two toroidal superconducting structures coupled via a quantized Aharonov-Bohm-type vector potential mediated by a superconducting loop threading both toroids; the loop remains in its ground state and enforces a global fluxoid constraint. The scheme uses correlated, time-resolved SQUID readout to observe flux exchange between remote toroids.
AI.result: A direct experimental signature would be correlated, time-resolved flux exchange between remote toroids observable via SQUID readout. The interaction presents an apparent signaling paradox related to nonlocal quantum coherence.
AI.conclusion: The proposed experimental testbed can address foundational questions about the existence of objective collapse, the fundamental limits of macroscopic quantum coherence, and constraints relevant to large-scale quantum computers.

title: Quantum state localization in dipole-dipole interacting disordered networks
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures. Supplementary material included (7 pages, 5 figures)
summary: We study the localization of excitations in positionally disordered spin or atom networks coupled via the realistic resonant dipole-dipole interaction (RDDI), which does not conform to a simple power law, as the spatial dependence and dissipative character distinguish it from conventional short or long-range models. Despite its partially long-ranged and radiative nature, positional disorder in the RDDI coupling leads to strong spatial localization of excitations. The interplay between coherent and dissipative couplings gives rise to nontrivial interference effects that stabilize localized modes even in open geometries. Our results uncover a photon wavelength-induced transition from extended to localized excitation dynamics, establishing RDDI networks as a unique setting to explore the emergence of localization in realistic quantum optical systems. Our analysis of the localized modes induced by RDDI has potential applications in coherent photovoltaics, excitonic circuits, quantum memory, and quantum sensors.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that positional disorder in resonant dipole-dipole interaction (RDDI) networks leads to strong spatial localization of excitations, with a photon wavelength-induced transition from extended to localized dynamics, despite the long-range and dissipative nature of RDDI.
AI.motivation: To understand how localization of excitations occurs in positionally disordered spin/atom networks coupled via realistic RDDI, which differs from conventional short or long-range models due to its spatial dependence and dissipative character.
AI.method: The authors study positional disorder in RDDI-coupled spin/atom networks, analyzing the interplay between coherent and dissipative couplings and their effects on excitation localization.
AI.result: Positional disorder in RDDI coupling leads to strong spatial localization of excitations; nontrivial interference effects from coherent-dissipative coupling interplay stabilize localized modes even in open geometries; a photon wavelength-induced transition from extended to localized dynamics is discovered.
AI.conclusion: RDDI networks represent a unique platform for exploring localization in realistic quantum optical systems, with potential applications in coherent photovoltaics, excitonic circuits, quantum memory, and quantum sensors.

title: Wilczek-Zee Realization of Uhlmann Parallel Transport
summary: The Uhlmann phase extends geometric phases to mixed quantum states via a parallel-transport condition on purification amplitudes, yet its direct implementation under standard Hamiltonian dynamics is obstructed by the non-Hermitian nature of the purification. We establish that for any smooth one-dimensional closed loop of full-rank qubit density matrices, there exists a four-level Hermitian parent Hamiltonian whose doubly degenerate ground-state subspace carries a Wilczek--Zee connection exactly equal to the Uhlmann connection. Consequently, the Uhlmann holonomy is faithfully reproduced by adiabatic evolution in the enlarged system. We further prove that this auxiliary-field construction is obstructed in generic two-dimensional parameter spaces by a Frobenius integrability condition, which we derive explicitly. The one-dimensional Uhlmann phase is thus placed on the same footing as the non-Abelian Berry phase, offering a purely Hermitian, Hamiltonian-based route to simulating mixed-state geometric phases. Numerical integration of the adiabatic dynamics confirms the exact correspondence and validates the convergence to the Uhlmann holonomy in the large-gap limit.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the Uhlmann phase for mixed qubit states can be realized via a Hermitian parent Hamiltonian's degenerate ground-state subspace, with the Uhlmann connection reproduced by the Wilczek–Zee connection in 1D, but obstructed in 2D by a Frobenius integrability condition.
AI.motivation: The Uhlmann phase, a geometric phase for mixed quantum states, has been difficult to implement under standard Hamiltonian dynamics because it relies on non-Hermitian purification constraints. This work aims to bridge that gap by providing a Hermitian, Hamiltonian-based framework.
AI.method: For any smooth 1D closed loop of full-rank qubit density matrices, a four-level Hermitian parent Hamiltonian is constructed whose doubly degenerate ground subspace encodes the Uhlmann connection as a Wilczek–Zee connection. The method includes a Frobenius integrability analysis for 2D parameter spaces and numerical adiabatic dynamics simulations.
AI.result: The Uhlmann holonomy is exactly reproduced by adiabatic evolution in the enlarged system for 1D loops. In 2D, a Frobenius integrability condition obstructs a similar construction. Numerical simulations confirm convergence to the Uhlmann holonomy in the large-gap limit.
AI.conclusion: The one-dimensional Uhlmann phase is placed on equal theoretical footing with the non-Abelian Berry phase, enabling a purely Hermitian simulation of mixed-state geometric phases, with clear limitations in higher-dimensional parameter spaces.

title: Contractivity of the Hilbert--Schmidt Speed in Unital Quantum Channels: Foundation for Witnessing Non-Markovianity and Discriminating Unital from Non-Unital Markovian Dynamics
summary: We investigate the Hilbert--Schmidt speed (HSS), a geometric indicator defined through the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of the tangent vector to a parametrized family of quantum states, under general open-system dynamics. Working in the framework of finite-dimensional, parameter-independent completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) evolution where the parameter is encoded solely in the initial state, we prove that the HSS is contractive under every unital CPTP map. Consequently, for any CP-divisible evolution whose intermediate propagators are unital, the HSS is monotonically non-increasing in time. We then establish the generator-level counterpart for Markovian dynamics governed by a Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) master equation with Hermitian Lindblad operators, deriving an explicit non-positive expression for the time derivative of the squared HSS. These results provide a rigorous foundation for using HSS backflow as a sufficient witness of non-Markovianity in physical settings where the relevant CP-divisible Markovian dynamics is known \emph{a priori} to be unital. Conversely, we show by an explicit qutrit counterexample that HSS can increase even in perfectly Markovian but non-unital dynamics, demonstrating that HSS non-monotonicity is not, in general, a faithful indicator of memory effects unless unitality is guaranteed. Our findings clarify the exact scope of HSS-based diagnostics and identify unitality as the crucial structural ingredient underlying their validity.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that Hilbert-Schmidt speed (HSS) is contractive under unital CPTP maps and monotonically non-increasing under CP-divisible unital evolutions, deriving an explicit non-positive derivative for GKSL master equations with Hermitian Lindblad operators. It shows HSS backflow can witness non-Markovianity only when dynamics are a priori known to be unital, and demonstrates via a qutrit counterexample that HSS can increase in Markovian non-unital dynamics, thus clarifying the scope of HSS-based non-Markovianity diagnostics.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish the theoretical foundations for using Hilbert-Schmidt speed (HSS) as a witness of non-Markovianity in open quantum systems, and to clarify the exact conditions under which HSS non-monotonicity reliably indicates memory effects versus being an artifact of non-unital dynamics.
AI.method: The authors work within the framework of finite-dimensional, parameter-independent CPTP evolution where the parameter is encoded solely in the initial state. They prove contractivity of HSS under unital CPTP maps, establish monotonicity for CP-divisible unital evolutions, derive a generator-level expression for the time derivative of squared HSS under GKSL dynamics with Hermitian Lindblad operators, and construct a qutrit counterexample of Markovian non-unital dynamics where HSS increases.
AI.result: HSS is contractive under every unital CPTP map. For CP-divisible evolutions with unital intermediate propagators, HSS is monotonically non-increasing. An explicit non-positive expression for the time derivative of squared HSS is derived for GKSL master equations with Hermitian Lindblad operators. A qutrit counterexample shows HSS can increase in Markovian non-unital dynamics.
AI.conclusion: HSS backflow can serve as a sufficient witness of non-Markovianity only when the relevant CP-divisible Markovian dynamics is known a priori to be unital. HSS non-monotonicity is not a faithful indicator of memory effects unless unitality is guaranteed. Unitality is identified as the crucial structural ingredient underlying the validity of HSS-based diagnostics.

title: Spin-1 teleportation-based quantum state tomography
summary: We show that the teleportation-based quantum state tomography (QST) protocol, originally built to reconstruct qubits (spin-1/2 systems), can be extended to deal with qutrits (spin-1 systems) as well. Similarly to the original proposal, only two resources are needed to implement the spin-1 teleportation-based QST protocol: (1) Alice should be able to implement the analog of Bell measurements for spin-1 systems; and (2) she should be able to prepare a few different single qutrit states that will be teleported to Bob.

AI.tldr: The paper extends the teleportation-based quantum state tomography (QST) protocol from qubits (spin-1/2) to qutrits (spin-1 systems), requiring only Bell measurements for spin-1 and preparation of single qutrit states.
AI.motivation: To generalize the teleportation-based QST protocol, originally designed for qubits, to work with higher-dimensional quantum systems (qutrits/spin-1 systems).
AI.method: The protocol extends the original teleportation-based QST framework by adapting it to spin-1 systems, requiring two resources: (1) analog of Bell measurements for spin-1 systems, and (2) preparation of a few different single qutrit states to be teleported to Bob.
AI.result: The teleportation-based QST protocol can successfully be extended from qubits to qutrits while requiring only the same two types of resources (Bell-like measurements and state preparation).
AI.conclusion: The teleportation-based QST protocol is not limited to qubits but can be generalized to higher-dimensional systems such as qutrits, using analogous resources.

title: Towards Quantum Network Performance Metrics: Challenges and Demonstration
summary: As quantum networks move toward practical deployment, standardized performance monitoring becomes essential. This article proposes a structured monitoring framework for quantum networks with performance metrics, including quality (e.g., entanglement fidelity, QBER, loss, dark count rate), throughput and latency (e.g., entanglement rate, waiting time), timing (e.g., coincidence window, production and coincidence jitter), and exogenous factors (e.g., temperature, humidity, vibrations). These measurements enable real-time observability, benchmarking, and control, supporting use cases such as fault diagnosis, adaptive timing, and entanglement routing. Additionally, we implement a non-invasive prototype environmental monitoring system integrated with the quantum network infrastructure at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, demonstrating practical feasibility of live data collection and alert generation. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges of real-time monitoring and the trade-offs between observability and system performance. This work establishes a foundation for developing advanced quantum network monitoring systems and lays the groundwork for future autonomous control and quantum software-defined networking.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a structured monitoring framework for quantum networks with metrics covering quality, throughput/latency, timing, and exogenous factors, and demonstrates a non-invasive prototype at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
AI.motivation: As quantum networks move toward practical deployment, standardized performance monitoring becomes essential for ensuring reliability and operational control.
AI.method: The authors define a multi-category metric framework (quality, throughput/latency, timing, exogenous factors) and implement a non-invasive environmental monitoring prototype integrated with quantum network infrastructure at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
AI.result: Demonstrated practical feasibility of live data collection and alert generation via the prototype system; identified trade-offs between observability and system performance.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a foundation for developing advanced quantum network monitoring systems and lays groundwork for future autonomous control and quantum software-defined networking.

title: Coherent Control of Channel Dilations Activate Temporal Bell Nonclassicality
summary: The temporal Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality witnesses the nonclassicality of temporal correlations, but its violation is generally degraded by environmental noise. Here, we show that violation of the temporal CHSH inequality can be revived through coherent control of noisy quantum evolutions. We compare two physically distinct implementations: coherent control of noisy evolutions induced by interaction of the system with independent environments, and coherent control of two physically distinct, unitarily equivalent Stinespring dilations of the same noisy channel. Although these constructions generate identical deterministic system dynamics, they induce distinctly different post-selected evolutions. With a focus on the amplitude damping channel (ADC), we show that coherent control of equivalent dilations extend the range of temporal CHSH inequality violation well beyond both the incoherently controlled, or deterministic, scenario and what is achievable with independent environments. Under setting-independent post-selection of the coherent control implementation, the resulting violation further certifies that the channel is not strongly CHSH nonlocality-breaking. Our results identify the choice of Stinespring dilation as an operationally relevant resource in coherently controlled tests of temporal quantum correlations.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that violation of the temporal CHSH inequality, typically degraded by noise, can be revived by coherently controlling noisy quantum evolutions. Two implementations are compared—coherent control of independent environments vs. coherent control of equivalent Stinespring dilations of the same channel. The latter extends violation ranges significantly beyond incoherent/deterministic scenarios and, under setting-independent post-selection, certifies the channel is not strongly CHSH nonlocality-breaking.
AI.motivation: Temporal CHSH inequality violation witnesses nonclassical temporal correlations, but environmental noise degrades this violation. The authors aim to revive and extend the violation range via coherent control of noisy evolutions, and to identify the Stinespring dilation choice as an operationally relevant resource.
AI.method: The paper compares two coherent control implementations: (1) coherent control of noisy evolutions from system interaction with independent environments, and (2) coherent control of two physically distinct but unitarily equivalent Stinespring dilations of the same noisy channel. The amplitude damping channel (ADC) is used as the test case.
AI.result: Coherent control of equivalent Stinespring dilations extends the temporal CHSH inequality violation range beyond both incoherent/deterministic scenarios and independent-environment implementations. Setting-independent post-selection yields violation that certifies the channel is not strongly CHSH nonlocality-breaking.
AI.conclusion: The Stinespring dilation choice is an operationally relevant resource in coherently controlled tests of temporal quantum correlations, enabling revival and extension of nonclassical temporal correlation signatures despite environmental noise.

title: Verifiable blind quantum computing: Comparative analysis and design considerations for client architectures
summary: Blind quantum computing (BQC) allows a client to delegate quantum computations to a remote server without revealing the input, computation, or output. In addition to being blind, the client can sometimes also verify that the server has performed their instructions correctly, a property known as verifiability. A key part of realizing such verifiable BQC (VBQC) is choosing the design of the client device: many architectures have been proposed, each with different hardware requirements, security properties, and performance characteristics, making it difficult to identify which is most suitable for a given implementation. In this work, we present a comparative analysis of client architectures for VBQC with a matter-qubit server. We restrict our analysis to single-server, single-client protocols with information-theoretic security based on measurement-based quantum computation. We identify three main categories of client: emission-based, measurement-based, and rotation-based, each with multiple variants depending on how the client interacts with the server. We evaluate each across different dimensions: we compare guarantees of existing corresponding security proofs, we derive equations for the rate at which each client can execute a protocol, we provide an overview of each architecture's error behaviour, and discuss hardware cost and design considerations. Client architectures implementing measurement-based remote state preparation and reflection-based teleportation emerge as strong default candidates, but as the right choice remains context-dependent, we provide a framework for navigating considerations to guide the selection of the most suitable architecture for a given setting.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a comparative analysis of client architectures for verifiable blind quantum computing (VBQC) with a matter-qubit server, categorizing them into emission-based, measurement-based, and rotation-based types, and evaluating them across security, rate, error behavior, and hardware considerations to guide architecture selection.
AI.motivation: Many VBQC client architectures exist with differing hardware requirements, security properties, and performance, making it difficult to identify the most suitable design for a given implementation. This work aims to systematically compare and provide guidance for architecture selection.
AI.method: The authors restrict analysis to single-server, single-client, information-theoretically secure VBQC protocols based on measurement-based quantum computation. They identify three client categories (emission-based, measurement-based, rotation-based) and evaluate them across security proofs, execution rates, error behaviors, and hardware cost/design considerations.
AI.result: Client architectures using measurement-based remote state preparation and reflection-based teleportation emerge as strong default candidates. The authors provide a framework for navigating context-dependent considerations to guide architecture selection.
AI.conclusion: No single architecture is universally optimal; the right choice remains context-dependent. The framework helps practitioners select the most suitable VBQC client architecture for their specific setting.

title: Interplay Between Quantum Coherence and Multiparameter Quantum Estimation in Graphene
summary: In this work, we investigate the relationship between quantum coherence and multiparameter quantum estimation in a graphene-based system. We focus on the estimation of two relevant physical parameters, namely the temperature $T$ and the wave vector $k_x$, and analyze how their variations affect both quantum coherence and the achievable metrological precision. The minimum variances associated with the estimation process are evaluated through the quantum Cramér--Rao bound within both simultaneous and independent estimation schemes. Our results show that quantum coherence is enhanced in the low-temperature regime and around $k_x=0$, while it decreases progressively as either the temperature or the wave vector increases. However, the regions where coherence is maximal do not necessarily coincide with those of optimal estimation precision. In particular, the variance associated with temperature estimation exhibits a divergent behavior near $T=0$, indicating that the system becomes weakly sensitive to small temperature variations in this regime. By contrast, the estimation of the wave vector $k_x$ is more directly related to the coherence properties of the system, with improved precision obtained near $k_x=0$. Furthermore, we introduce the ratio $Γ$ to compare the total variances obtained from the independent and simultaneous estimation schemes. This quantity provides a useful measure of the relative difference between the two strategies when the parameters are estimated separately or jointly.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the link between quantum coherence and multiparameter estimation in graphene, finding that coherence peaks at low T and k_x=0, but optimal estimation precision does not always align with maximal coherence. Temperature estimation diverges near T=0 while wave vector estimation aligns better with coherence. A ratio Γ compares independent vs. simultaneous estimation schemes.
AI.motivation: To investigate the relationship between quantum coherence and multiparameter quantum estimation in a graphene-based system, specifically examining how coherence relates to the achievable precision in estimating temperature T and wave vector k_x.
AI.method: The study evaluates minimum variances using the quantum Cramér–Rao bound for both simultaneous and independent estimation schemes. A ratio Γ is introduced to compare total variances from the two estimation strategies.
AI.result: Quantum coherence is enhanced at low T and around k_x=0, and decreases with increasing T or k_x. Regions of maximal coherence do not align with optimal estimation precision. Temperature estimation variance diverges near T=0, while wave vector estimation precision improves near k_x=0.
AI.conclusion: Quantum coherence and estimation precision are not strictly correlated in this graphene system; the wave vector estimation is more directly tied to coherence than temperature estimation. The ratio Γ provides a useful metric for comparing independent vs. simultaneous multiparameter estimation performance.

title: Entangled quantum clocks as operational probes of spacetime curvature
summary: Building on the framework developed by Perche [Phys. Rev. D 106, 025018 (2022)], we study two localized nonrelativistic quantum particles propagating along timelike geodesics in a curved spacetime background. Each particle is coupled to a quantum clock that operationally records the time spent in a prescribed spatial region. We compute the covariance of the resulting time observables for separable and entangled two-particle states, comparing flat and curved backgrounds. We then reformulate the protocol as a Bell-like experiment and show that the Bell parameter can acquire a curvature-induced correction. In particular, a protocol calibrated to saturate the classical bound in flat spacetime can be driven above this bound in curved spacetime for entangled states. We focus on two-dimensional curved backgrounds in which the local tidal term induces an effective harmonic potential in the Fermi-frame description. Our results show that spacetime curvature can modify operationally defined quantum correlations and suggest entangled quantum clocks as probes of spacetime curvature.

AI.tldr: The paper studies two localized quantum particles with quantum clocks in curved spacetime, showing that spacetime curvature can modify Bell-like correlations and drive entangled states above the classical bound.
AI.motivation: To investigate how spacetime curvature affects operationally defined temporal correlations between quantum clocks coupled to particles moving along timelike geodesics, and to explore whether entangled quantum clocks can serve as probes of spacetime curvature.
AI.method: Using Perche's framework, the authors study two nonrelativistic quantum particles on timelike geodesics in curved spacetime, each coupled to a quantum clock recording time spent in a spatial region. They compute the covariance of time observables for separable and entangled states in flat vs. curved backgrounds, then reformulate as a Bell-like experiment with a curvature-dependent Bell parameter.
AI.result: The Bell parameter acquires a curvature-induced correction. A protocol calibrated to saturate the classical bound in flat spacetime can exceed this bound in curved spacetime for entangled states. The analysis is performed on two-dimensional curved backgrounds where the tidal term acts as an effective harmonic potential in the Fermi frame.
AI.conclusion: Spacetime curvature can modify operationally defined quantum correlations, suggesting that entangled quantum clocks can be used as probes of spacetime curvature.

title: Enhanced phase estimation with coherently boosted two-mode squeezed beams and its application to optical gyroscopes
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures. Published in Phys. Rev. A 102, 022614 (2020)
summary: Quantum techniques, developed in recent decades, provide new approaches to achieving high-precision measurements beyond the classical bounds. In this paper, we theoretically demonstrate a metrology method for improving the sensitivity of the interferometric optical gyroscope, robust against the loss, by using coherent-light stimulated two-mode squeezed beams as the light source. The detection protocol is based on a simple intensity measurement, and the quantum noise is far below the shot-noise limit. The enhancement factors for different coherent light fields are analyzed in detail. Additionally, the influence of loss during the propagation in the optical path is studied, and the conditions for achieving sub-shot-noise measurement sensitivity are obtained. We also find that the phase sensitivity of the proposed gyroscope scheme becomes closer to the quantum Cramér-Rao bound with increasing of the photon number of the coherent beams.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a loss-robust interferometric optical gyroscope using coherent-light stimulated two-mode squeezed beams and simple intensity measurement, achieving sub-shot-noise sensitivity approaching the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
AI.motivation: To overcome the classical shot-noise limit and improve the sensitivity of interferometric optical gyroscopes while maintaining robustness against optical loss, using quantum techniques.
AI.method: The method employs coherent-light stimulated two-mode squeezed beams as the light source in an interferometric gyroscope, with a simple intensity measurement detection protocol. The analysis includes enhancement factors for different coherent light fields and the effect of propagation loss.
AI.result: The proposed scheme achieves quantum noise far below the shot-noise limit, with phase sensitivity approaching the quantum Cramér-Rao bound as the photon number of coherent beams increases. Conditions for achieving sub-shot-noise measurement sensitivity under loss are also obtained.
AI.conclusion: Coherent-light stimulated two-mode squeezed beams enable loss-robust, high-sensitivity gyroscope measurements beyond classical limits, with simple intensity-based detection.

title: Many-body quantum optics in a cascaded chiral network
summary: Chiral quantum emitters interact with light only in one propagation direction, allowing them to be linked into cascaded systems in which photons mediate ordered, long-range interactions. Such systems are predicted to host novel regimes of many-body physics of light and matter. Exploring these regimes requires arrays of identical quantum emitters with directional, low-loss coupling to guided photons, a combination that has thus far remained experimentally out of reach. Here we realize a cascaded network of superconducting qubits using an architecture that overcomes these bottlenecks. We implement a four-qubit chain spanning two modules, with separations ranging from millimeters to half a meter, and exploit the shared waveguide as a dissipative resource to stabilize reconfigurable entanglement, reaching a genuinely multipartite regime unavailable in reciprocal baths. By scattering weak pulses off the chain, we observe photons sorted in time by photon number, a signature of the strong photon-photon interactions mediated by the emitters. Together, these results provide experimental access to many-body light-matter regimes that are beyond the reach of reciprocal systems.

AI.tldr: The paper realizes a cascaded network of superconducting qubits coupled directionally to a common waveguide, demonstrating reconfigurable multipartite entanglement and photon-number-dependent temporal sorting of photons, enabling access to many-body physics unavailable in reciprocal systems.
AI.motivation: To experimentally realize cascaded quantum systems (where chiral emitters interact unidirectionally with light) which are predicted to host novel many-body light-matter physics but have remained experimentally out of reach due to the need for identical emitters with directional, low-loss coupling to guided photons.
AI.method: Using superconducting qubits in a cascaded network architecture with a shared waveguide as a dissipative resource, implementing a four-qubit chain spanning two modules with separations from millimeters to half a meter, and scattering weak pulses off the chain.
AI.result: Demonstrated stabilization of reconfigurable multipartite entanglement (a genuinely multipartite regime unavailable in reciprocal baths) and observed photons sorted in time by photon number, indicating strong photon-photon interactions mediated by the emitters.
AI.conclusion: The results provide experimental access to many-body light-matter regimes that are beyond the reach of reciprocal systems, opening the door to exploring novel quantum many-body physics with cascaded quantum networks.

title: Separating transient leakage exposure from endpoint cancellation in fast transmon single-qubit gates
summary: Fast single-qubit gates on weakly anharmonic transmons are limited by leakage to noncomputational states, and standard mitigations such as DRAG (derivative removal by adiabatic gate) act on the leakage amplitude at the end of the gate. We show that this endpoint amplitude and the transient leakage exposure accumulated during the gate are two distinct control objectives that can be assigned to separate modules. The endpoint is a single sample of the drive spectrum, $|\tildeΛ(η)|^2$; the exposure is a band integral about $η$ and governs leakage under dephasing, and the spectral-null condition $\tildeΛ(η)=0$ constrains only the former. We realize this split in a path--endpoint separation pulse (PESP): a path-shaping pulse suppresses the exposure, and a two-tone endpoint-cancellation pulse cancels the residual amplitude. For a $10$ ns $R_{X}(π/2)$ gate at $η/2π=0.2$ GHz, in numerical simulations the path-shaping pulse reduces the dephasing exposure by ${\sim}21\%$ relative to cosine DRAG and the independently simulated Lindblad excess leakage by ${\sim}20\%$, consistent with $P_{\mathrm{excess}}^φ\simeqγ_φT\bar{P}_{A}^{\mathrm{deph}}$, whereas matched-budget endpoint-only and spectral-null controls leave it essentially unchanged. The residual endpoint floor splits exactly into a $|2\rangle$ back-action and a $|3\rangle$ cascade, which the two tones cancel one-to-one, driving the floor at the path-exposure knee from ${\sim}7\times10^{-7}$ to ${\sim}3\times10^{-8}$ without perturbing the path. By separating transient exposure from endpoint leakage, PESP turns leakage suppression in fast weakly anharmonic gates into a modular, interpretable control problem: dephasing-induced leakage and the coherent residual error are reduced by separate, individually verifiable modules.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Path-Endpoint Separation Pulse (PESP), a modular approach to leakage suppression in fast single-qubit gates on weakly anharmonic transmons, separating endpoint leakage amplitude from transient leakage exposure and addressing each with distinct control modules.
AI.motivation: Fast single-qubit gates on weakly anharmonic transmons suffer from leakage to noncomputational states. Standard mitigations like DRAG only address leakage amplitude at the gate endpoint, but transient leakage accumulated during the gate (especially under dephasing) is a distinct and unaddressed problem.
AI.method: PESP splits leakage suppression into two modules: a path-shaping pulse that suppresses transient leakage exposure (a band integral about the qubit-anharmonicity frequency η), and a two-tone endpoint-cancellation pulse that cancels residual endpoint amplitude. The endpoint amplitude is shown to be a single spectral sample |Λ̃(η)|², while exposure is a band integral governing dephasing-induced leakage.
AI.result: For a 10 ns R_X(π/2) gate at η/2π=0.2 GHz, path-shaping reduces dephasing exposure by ~21% and Lindblad excess leakage by ~20% relative to cosine DRAG. The two-tone cancellation drives the residual endpoint floor from ~7×10⁻⁷ to ~3×10⁻⁸. Endpoint-only and spectral-null controls leave dephasing leakage essentially unchanged.
AI.conclusion: By separating transient exposure from endpoint leakage, PESP turns leakage suppression into a modular, interpretable control problem where dephasing-induced leakage and coherent residual error are reduced by separate, individually verifiable modules.

title: A Quantum-HPC Hybrid Workflow for Reaction-Center Electronic Dynamics: Application to a Cytochrome P450-Inspired Iron-Complex Model
summary: We introduce population-transfer dynamics as a practical validation observable for active-space-derived reduced Hamiltonians in multistate reaction-center chemistry. Using a cytochrome P450-inspired Fe-complex model, we construct a reaction-coordinate-dependent effective Hamiltonian from state-averaged complete active-space self-consistent field (SA-CASSCF) calculations, map it to a quantum-circuit representation suitable for current hardware, and propagate dynamics from the reactant-side ground state. The reduced Hamiltonian reproduces the SA-CASSCF reference with an RMS deviation of 0.030 eV and a maximum absolute deviation of 0.143 eV. As a dynamics-based diagnostic, the product-manifold population p_P(t) identifies a pronounced near-degeneracy region around x = 0.3, where state mixing is strongest. Classical exact time evolution yields a product population of 0.488 at x = 0.3 after 10 fs, compared with 7.26 x 10^-2 at x = 0.2 and 5.90 x 10^-3 at x = 0.0. To enable execution on current trapped-ion hardware, we examine the trade-off between dynamical fidelity and circuit resources through coupling pruning and first-order Trotterization. A coupling cutoff of 0.02 eV reduces the non-zero coupling set from 32 to 7 while preserving the dominant transfer pathways, and M = 30 provides the best practical operating point. Finally, we demonstrate the workflow on Quantinuum's trapped-ion quantum computer Reimei. The hardware reproduces the key reaction-coordinate trend identified by the classical model, including the maximum at x = 0.3, where the measured product population is 0.42 on hardware and 0.43 on the matched emulator. This work establishes a dynamics-based framework for assessing active-space-derived reduced Hamiltonians and demonstrates chemically interpretable multistate electronic dynamics on current trapped-ion hardware.

The reduced Hamiltonian is constructed from SA-CASSCF calculations, mapped to a quantum-circuit representation, and dynamics are propagated. The workflow is demonstrated on Quantinuum's trapped-ion quantum computer Reimei, showing that hardware reproduces key reaction-coordinate trends, including a pronounced near-degeneracy region at x=0.3.

A coupling cutoff of 0.02 eV reduces couplings from 32 to 7. On Reimei, the hardware yields product population 0.42 at x=0.3 vs 0.43 on the matched emulator.

title: Latency-Constrained Hardware-Aware Quantum Error Correction Co-Design with Adaptive Confidence-Gated Neural Decoding for the Rotated Surface Code
comment: 29 pages, 18 figures, 12 tables. Source code, trained models, and benchmark data: https://github.com/Sumitchongder/adaptive-qec-decoder
summary: Real-time decoding is a major bottleneck in scaling quantum error correction (QEC) from noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices to fault-tolerant quantum computing. We present an adaptive confidence-gated decoding framework for the rotated surface code that treats decoding as a two-stage inference problem. A lightweight feed-forward neural network performs fast-path decoding for the majority of syndrome measurements, while only low-confidence predictions are escalated to a minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) refinement stage. We benchmark the framework on rotated surface codes with distances $d \in \{3,5,7,9,11\}$ under circuit-level depolarising noise using the Stim stabiliser simulator. The evaluation characterises logical accuracy, confidence-controlled accuracy-latency trade-offs, decoding throughput, per-shot latency, and decoding-graph resource scaling. Routing only 3.3%-6.2% of syndromes to the refinement stage improves logical accuracy from 99.21% for the neural-only baseline to 99.81% at a confidence threshold of 0.95 while incurring only a bounded increase in average decoding cost. Neural-decoder throughput saturates near $4.6 \times 10^{5}$ samples s$^{-1}$ at batch size 512 on commodity CPU hardware, indicating that the neural fast path is not the dominant throughput bottleneck beyond code distance $d=7$. We release the complete benchmarking pipeline, trained models, raw benchmark data, and source code, and explicitly distinguish the experimentally validated contributions from the broader hardware-aware QEC co-design roadmap, including hardware-constrained code discovery, GPU-accelerated inference, and multi-noise optimisation, which remain directions for future work.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an adaptive confidence-gated decoding framework for the rotated surface code that uses a lightweight neural network for fast-path decoding of most syndrome measurements, with only low-confidence predictions escalated to MWPM refinement. This achieves 99.81% logical accuracy at 0.95 confidence threshold while routing only 3.3%-6.2% of syndromes to refinement, and neural decoder throughput reaches ~4.6×10⁵ samples/s on commodity CPU.
AI.motivation: Real-time decoding is a major bottleneck in scaling quantum error correction from NISQ devices to fault-tolerant quantum computing, motivating the need for efficient decoding architectures that balance accuracy and latency.
AI.method: The authors propose a two-stage confidence-gated decoding framework: (1) a lightweight feed-forward neural network performs fast-path decoding for most syndrome measurements, (2) only low-confidence predictions are escalated to a minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) refinement stage. The framework is benchmarked on rotated surface codes with distances d∈{3,5,7,9,11} under circuit-level depolarising noise using the Stim simulator.
AI.result: Routing only 3.3%-6.2% of syndromes to MWPM refinement improves logical accuracy from 99.21% (neural-only baseline) to 99.81% at a confidence threshold of 0.95. Neural-decoder throughput saturates near 4.6×10⁵ samples/s at batch size 512 on commodity CPU, and the neural fast path is not the dominant throughput bottleneck beyond code distance d=7.
AI.conclusion: The confidence-gated framework provides effective accuracy-latency trade-offs for real-time QEC decoding. The neural fast path is not the limiting throughput bottleneck for larger code distances. The paper releases the complete benchmarking pipeline and explicitly distinguishes validated contributions from future hardware-aware QEC co-design directions.

title: Maximal coherence of quantum measurement and the resource theory of sharpness
summary: A resource theory of quantum measurement can be addressed in terms of quantum coherence and measurement sharpness, respectively. The former analyzes the off-diagonal structure of POVM elements in a predetermined basis while the latter analyzes the deviation from trivial, state-independent, measurements. We establish a direct connection between the two resource theories by identifying measurement sharpness as the maximal coherence that is achievable under all possible unitary changes of the reference basis. For a broad class of POVMs whose elements share a common eigenbasis, we show that the maximal distance-based coherence of measurement coincides exactly with the corresponding distance-based sharpness monotone. We further extend this equivalence, with element-additive distances, to POVMs whose elements admit a common mutually unbiased basis structure. These results provide a measurement-theoretic analogue of the maximal-coherence \& purity correspondence for quantum states. We also show that the maximal coherence of measurement is faithful with respect to trivial measurements and is monotonic under fuzzifying operations for dichotomic measurements, as well as under mixed-unitary and unitarily covariant preprocessing channels. Finally, we illustrate the operational meaning and limitations of the equivalence through qubit POVMs, single-photon phase sensing, and noisy photon-number resolving detection. In particular, the maximal Fisher information in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer is shown to be determined by the squared maximal coherence of the measurement, while in an imperfect photon-number resolving detector the maximal coherence behaves as a proper sharpness monotone, unlike conventional PVM-based unsharpness measures.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a direct equivalence between two resource theories of quantum measurement—quantum coherence of POVM elements (off-diagonal structure) and measurement sharpness (deviation from trivial measurements)—by showing that sharpness is the maximal coherence achievable under all unitary basis changes. This equivalence is proven for POVMs with a common eigenbasis and extended to those with a common mutually unbiased basis structure, and is illustrated through qubit POVMs, phase sensing, and noisy photon detection.
AI.motivation: To bridge two previously separate resource theories of quantum measurement—coherence-based and sharpness-based—by establishing their direct equivalence, analogous to the known coherence-purity correspondence for quantum states.
AI.method: The authors identify measurement sharpness as the maximal coherence achievable under all unitary transformations of the reference basis. They prove the equivalence for distance-based measures for POVMs with a common eigenbasis, and extend it to POVMs with a common mutually unbiased basis (MUB) structure using element-additive distances. They also analyze monotonicity under fuzzifying operations, mixed-unitary channels, and unitarily covariant preprocessing.
AI.result: For POVMs sharing a common eigenbasis, the maximal distance-based coherence equals the corresponding sharpness monotone. The equivalence extends to MUB-structured POVMs with element-additive distances. The maximal coherence is faithful (vanishes only for trivial measurements) and monotonic under certain operations. The maximal Fisher information in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer is determined by the squared maximal coherence, and for noisy photon-number resolving detectors, maximal coherence behaves as a proper sharpness monotone unlike conventional PVM-based measures.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a measurement-theoretic analogue of the maximal-coherence & purity correspondence for quantum states, unifying two resource theories and offering operational interpretations in quantum metrology and detection scenarios.

title: Hidden Complex Structure in Quotient-Space Real Quantum Mechanics
summary: Barrios Hita et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. $\bf{136}$, 240202 (2026)] argued that quantum mechanics can be formulated over the real numbers by replacing the tensor-product postulate with a quotient-space construction, and concluded that complex numbers are therefore a matter of convenience. We show that the operational content of this construction is not that of a generic real Hilbert-space theory. Empirical equivalence requires a distinguished real linear operator $J$ with $J^2 = -\mathbb{1}$, and all physical effects, instruments, and dynamics must preserve the corresponding $SO(2)$ gauge. Moreover, the composite-system rule is a balanced tensor product over this hidden complex structure, not the ordinary tensor product over $\mathbb{R}$. In multipartite network scenarios, this changes the meaning of source independence: canonical real representatives are not source-factorizable in the usual tensor-product sense. Thus, the construction is best understood as standard complex quantum mechanics written in real notation, not as an independent real-amplitude theory. This clarifies what is, and is not, excluded by experiments testing the necessity of complex numbers.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the real-number formulation of quantum mechanics proposed by Barrios Hita et al. is operationally equivalent to standard complex quantum mechanics, requiring a hidden complex structure (a J operator) that imposes SO(2) gauge constraints on all physical elements, and uses a balanced tensor product rather than a standard real tensor product. Thus it does not constitute an independent real-amplitude theory, clarifying what experiments testing complex numbers actually rule out.
AI.motivation: To critically examine a recent claim that quantum mechanics can be formulated over real numbers, replacing the tensor-product postulate with a quotient-space construction, and to determine whether this construction truly represents an independent real-amplitude theory or is merely complex quantum mechanics in real notation.
AI.method: Operational analysis of the quotient-space construction proposed by Barrios Hita et al., examining the required mathematical structures (J operator, SO(2) gauge, balanced tensor product) and the implications for source independence in multipartite network scenarios.
AI.result: The construction requires a distinguished real operator J with J² = -𝟙; all physical effects, instruments, and dynamics must preserve an SO(2) gauge; the composite-system rule is a balanced tensor product over this hidden complex structure, not the ordinary real tensor product; canonical real representatives are not source-factorizable in the usual tensor-product sense in multipartite networks.
AI.conclusion: The construction is best understood as standard complex quantum mechanics written in real notation, not as an independent real-amplitude theory. This clarifies what experiments testing the necessity of complex numbers actually exclude.

title: Fixing Divergence in Carleman Linearization via Analytical Continuation
comment: 35 pages. 18 figures, this work is an extended version of a presentation delivered at the 16th Quantum Software Research Presentation Meeting
summary: Nonlinear differential equations play a crucial role in modeling a wide range of phenomena, yet their solutions remain notoriously difficult to obtain. With the rapid development of quantum computing, quantum algorithms for efficiently solving such equations are actively being explored. One promising approach is based on Carleman linearization, which transforms nonlinear differential equations into linear systems. However, this method suffers from exponential divergence beyond a certain time scale. By reformulating the solutions in terms of eigenvalues and eigenvectors, we identify that this divergence originates from the Laurent expansion outside its neighborhood of convergence. To address this issue, we insert a regularized function to the divergent solution hinted by analytical continuation. We validate this divergence-correction method on both the logistic equation and some other partial differential equations like KPP-Fisher equations and Phase-Field models under periodic conditions. We implement our method for the logistic equation using the Linear Combination of Unitaries (LCU) quantum algorithm, providing a detailed complexity and error analysis.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies that Carleman linearization for solving nonlinear differential equations on quantum computers diverges exponentially due to Laurent expansion outside its convergence radius, and proposes a divergence-correction method using analytical continuation with a regularized function, validated on logistic, KPP-Fisher, and Phase-Field equations with LCU quantum algorithm implementation.
AI.motivation: Nonlinear differential equations are crucial for modeling many phenomena but are difficult to solve. Quantum algorithms based on Carleman linearization suffer from exponential divergence beyond a certain time scale, limiting their applicability.
AI.method: The authors reformulate solutions in terms of eigenvalues/eigenvectors to identify the divergence origin (Laurent expansion outside its convergence neighborhood). They insert a regularized function guided by analytical continuation to correct the divergence, and implement the method using the Linear Combination of Unitaries (LCU) quantum algorithm.
AI.result: The divergence-correction method is validated on the logistic equation, KPP-Fisher equations, and Phase-Field models under periodic conditions. A detailed complexity and error analysis is provided for the LCU implementation on the logistic equation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed regularization via analytical continuation successfully mitigates the exponential divergence issue in Carleman linearization-based quantum algorithms for nonlinear differential equations, extending their practical applicability.

title: Strictly Local Tile-Code Architectures on Two-Dimensional Planar Lattices
summary: Tile codes are a family of planar quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with weight-6 stabilizers and open boundary conditions, offering an encoding efficiency $kd^2/n$ of up to four times that of the surface code. In this work, we develop an exhaustive search algorithm for finding SWAP-based routing schemes that implement syndrome extraction for four tile-code families using only nearest-neighbor interactions on a two-dimensional square lattice, matching the connectivity of the surface code. Using explicitly constructed routed syndrome-extraction circuits decoded with BP+OSD, we estimate the circuit-level thresholds of these code families.
